bank: EYES AND EARS -- E14 [late beat] -- THE BEAT vs THE JUDGE, SPEC ONLY
round: 1 of 2 (SCHOOL). Nothing built, nothing measured on our surface.
note: DRAFT MATERIAL, NEVER WIRED INTO THE GAME. School's corrections: (1) 'the gap' is not a number, it is a bias plus a jitter and it moves at runtime; (2) a tap test measures a HUMAN, not a phone, because people tap 20 to 100 ms EARLY and that bias is not even universal; (3) the browser reports the device's audio latency directly, so the audio half is a read, not a survey.

our_numbers_read_off_disk.the_problem: two grace values five times apart. until round two establishes which one the fight judges by, 'is the beat late' has no denominator. NO CLAIM is made here about which is right.

bluetooth_against_our_numbers.aptx_low_latency_best_case: 30-40 ms codec level, more system-wide, and only when both ends support it
bluetooth_against_our_numbers.against_grace_40: the SMALLEST realistic Bluetooth delay is about four whole windows late. impossible by construction, not hard.
bluetooth_against_our_numbers.against_grace_200: a typical 150-300 ms delay straddles the entire window; some devices land inside it by luck
bluetooth_against_our_numbers.the_worse_half: Bluetooth latency arrives AFTER calibration. a player calibrates on the speaker, puts headphones on, and the correction is now wrong by 200 ms.

the_browser_answers_the_audio_half.outputLatency: seconds between the browser handing a buffer to the host audio system and the first sample reaching the output device
the_browser_answers_the_audio_half.baseLatency: seconds of processing latency inside the graph, destination node into the host audio system
the_browser_answers_the_audio_half.getOutputTimestamp: contextTime (the sample frame playing now, audio clock) and performanceTime (the same instant in performance.now terms) -- it exists to bridge the two clock domains for games
the_browser_answers_the_audio_half.consequence: a calibration screen exists because native games cannot ask the device how late it is. on the web we can. the audio half is a READ.

the_human_taps_early.effect: negative mean asynchrony: finger taps typically PRECEDE the pacing sound
the_human_taps_early.reference: Repp, Sensorimotor synchronization: a review of the tapping literature
the_human_taps_early.and_it_is_not_universal: a cross-cultural study finds the effect is not universal, so it cannot be subtracted as a constant either
the_human_taps_early.consequence: every tap-based calibration measures device latency PLUS the player's anticipation and cannot separate them. MEASURE THE MACHINE WITH THE MACHINE. Never ask a human to calibrate a number a browser already reports.

two_offsets_not_one.audio: how late the sound leaves the device
two_offsets_not_one.real_examples: Rhythm Doctor calibrates in two phases (line up picture and sound, then a tap test for input); Chunithm names them Offset A and Offset B
two_offsets_not_one.the_classic_bug: the two get ADDED, so the game compensates for the sum rather than the true audio latency
two_offsets_not_one.consequence: round two says WHICH PAIR OF CLOCKS it measured instead of reporting 'the gap' as if there were one

order_of_operations.how: read outputLatency and baseLatency on the real surface at iPhone size in the shipped alpha
establish which grace the fight actually judges by, by reading the code path the fight runs, not by guessing between 200 and 40

order_of_operations.step: BEAT vs JUDGE, MACHINE TO MACHINE
order_of_operations.how: wrap the scheduler and the judge, collect many beats, report BIAS and JITTER and the worst beat, never one gap
drive taps exactly on the audio-clock beat corrected by outputLatency and see what the fight scores. no human, no calibration screen, no opinion.

order_of_operations.why: a window that survives a wired phone and dies on headphones is a finding the player meets on day one

rule_zero.trap: a simulated perfect player scoring 100% proves nothing on its own: it may mean the fight is fair, or that the judge is reading taps off the same clock that generated them, which is a tautology dressed as a pass
rule_zero.control: plant a DELIBERATELY LATE player, the same taps shifted by a known amount such as 150 ms, and the score MUST drop. if a 150 ms late player still scores perfect, the judge is not judging and every number is meaningless.
rule_zero.second_control: from E13: a sweep that interacts changes its own subject. driving taps into a fight changes the fight's state, so each run starts from a fresh fight.

what_players_and_games_get_wrong.why: watching the pulsing line makes players doubt their own rhythm; the advice is to close your eyes and listen for the accent. a calibration that SHOWS you something is measuring the wrong sense.
it moves the centre of the window, not the width of the error
osu! separates local from universal offset; conflating them fixes one song and breaks the rest

blind_spots_to_declare: one device, one browser, one output route: this measures the harness's audio path, not a real phone's
Bluetooth cannot be tested here at all; its numbers stay quoted, never measured
nothing here says whether the fight is FUN, which is his
what_this_lane_may_not_do: change any timing, window or offset (this lane never writes game code)
decide how hard the fight should be
